page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no margin notes. Printed page number 673 at the top right. Below the last line, a signature "Vu 4" at the left and a catchword "ne" at the right.

main_text.p: Quid hic ais Hottingere? Vides? Eoæ Ecclesiæ, Coptitæ, Melchitæ, Maronitæ, Iacobitæ, Nestorianæ sanctos Angelos, Prophetas, Apostolos, Martyres, Doctores, Iustos invocant, eorum operam implorant, & apud Deum patrocinium. Provinciæ, Urbes singulæ, Artes, Professiones sibi privatum unum aliquem ex illis, quem sibi magis profuturum existimant, advocatum, & monitorem asciscunt, & in rebus adversis propitium, & generalibus, & privatis precibus intercedunt, ut sanent animas, ut ipsos seruent, ut custodiant, ut eripiant a grauissimis afflictionibus, ut auxilia præbeant egentibus, ut auxilientur, ut concilient tranquillitatem, & pacem omnibus diebus, ut sibi a Deo obtineant remissionem peccatorum, ut infirmi sanentur, curentur, claudi ut ambulent, & erigantur ab auxilijs officium eorum, & tandem ne mergantur in mari perturbato peccatorum. Et potissimum Deiparam Virginem, quam, & gratia plenam, fidelium refugium, fortissimum Christianorum, Mundique auxilium, matrem vitæ, fontem deliciarum, per quem omnia bona euenere hominibus, & quid non in laudem eius non [illegible, ~8 letters], sed ὄντως[?] accumulant? ut offerat pro salute, & liberatio-
[illegible, ~8 letters]: the Greek word after "non" in the line "non in laudem eius non", printed in Greek letters, could not be read with certainty.

page.notes: The page is printed as a single block of text. Long s has been normalised to s throughout (for example "fanctos", "fibi", "faneht" and "fingulae" appear as printed with the long-s form and are given as sanctos, sibi, sanent and singulae). The word "afcifcunt" is read as "asciscunt" (adsciscunt in the classical form), but the scan is uncertain, so this reading is doubtful. The Greek word before "sed" is illegible at this resolution. The word "ὄντως" is a guess from context and is marked with [?]. The small mark at the bottom left is a stray printer's or scanner's mark, not text, and is omitted.
